name: Bādarāyaṇa

tradition.text: identical with Vyāsa, end of Dvāpara

notes: The identification with Vyāsa (tch:vyasa) is the tradition's; Śaṅkara refers to the sūtrakāra as Vyāsa in places. Scholars treat them as distinct.
summary: Author (tradition) or final redactor (scholarly) of the Brahma Sūtras; he states his own view by name at several points (e.g. BS 1.3.33, 3.4.1, 4.4.7, 4.4.12) against Jaimini, Bādari and others.

name: Vyāsa (Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana)
summary: In the Vedānta tradition, author of the Brahma Sūtras (as Bādarāyaṇa) and of the Mahābhārata and Purāṇas; in the Advaita guru-paramparā, son and disciple of Parāśara and teacher of his son Śuka; the Śaṅkaradigvijaya has him appear to Śaṅkara at Kāśī, test his commentary and extend his life.

name: Śuka (Śukadeva)
summary: Son and disciple of Vyāsa; in the Advaita guru-paramparā the teacher of Gauḍapāda (tradition), and a model of the born-free renunciant.

name: Jaimini
summary: Author of the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra; cited by name in the Brahma Sūtras for views Bādarāyaṇa records and often corrects: that knowledge is subsidiary to ritual (BS 3.4.2), that the gods are not eligible for the honey-meditation (1.3.31), that the path of the gods leads to the supreme Brahman (4.3.12), that the liberated has Brahman's qualities (4.4.5) and a body (4.4.11). Tradition makes him a disciple of Vyāsa.

name: Āśmarathya
summary: Early Vedāntin named in the Brahma Sūtras (1.2.29; 1.4.20). On the self and Brahman he held that the Upaniṣads' promise ('by knowing one, all is known') indicates non-difference; Śaṅkara glosses his view as difference-and-non-difference, like sparks and fire.

name: Auḍulomi
summary: Early Vedāntin named in the Brahma Sūtras (1.4.21; 3.4.45; 4.4.6): the individual self becomes one with Brahman when it departs (in liberation), being different while bound; the liberated self exists as pure consciousness alone.

name: Kāśakṛtsna
notes: A Kāśakṛtsna is also remembered in the grammatical tradition; identity uncertain.
summary: Early Vedāntin named in BS 1.4.22: the supreme self itself abides as the individual self. Śaṅkara declares Kāśakṛtsna's view to be the one in accord with scripture.

name: Bādari
summary: Early teacher cited in the Brahma Sūtras (1.2.30; 3.1.11; 4.3.7; 4.4.10) and in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra: the path of the gods leads to the conditioned (kārya) Brahman; the liberated has no body.

name: Kārṣṇājini
summary: Early teacher cited in BS 3.1.9 on the meaning of 'conduct' (caraṇa) in the Chāndogya's account of rebirth (as indicating residual karma).

name: Ātreya (of the Brahma Sūtras)
summary: Early teacher cited in BS 3.4.44: the fruit of meditations connected with ritual goes to the sacrificer (as owner), against Auḍulomi's view that it goes to the priest.

name: Upavarṣa
notes: Some later tradition identifies him with Bodhāyana the vṛttikāra; the Kathāsaritsāgara makes him a grammarian of Pāṭaliputra (low confidence).
summary: Ancient commentator on the Mīmāṃsā (and, by Śaṅkara's report, the one who deferred discussion of the self to the Śārīraka); Śaṅkara calls him 'bhagavān Upavarṣa' (BSBh 1.3.28; 3.3.53).

name: Bodhāyana (the Vṛttikāra)
summary: Author of an extensive vṛtti on the Brahma Sūtras which Rāmānuja says earlier teachers abridged and which he follows; claimed as a precursor of Viśiṣṭādvaita.

name: Brahmanandin (Ṭaṅka)
summary: Pre-Śaṅkara Vedāntin, the 'Vākyakāra', author of the Vākya cited by Yāmuna, Rāmānuja and others.

name: Dramiḍa (Draviḍācārya)
summary: Pre-Śaṅkara Vedāntin who commented on Brahmanandin's Vākya; cited by Rāmānuja as an authority.

name: Bhartṛprapañca
summary: Pre-Śaṅkara Vedāntin who held difference-and-non-difference between Brahman and the world/selves and taught that liberation requires knowledge combined with works; known through Śaṅkara's and Sureśvara's refutations in their Bṛhadāraṇyaka commentaries.

name: Brahmadatta
summary: Pre-Śaṅkara (or early) Vedāntin reported to have held that the knowledge from the Upaniṣads must be meditated upon throughout life (knowledge as an injunction to meditation) and that the individual self is not eternal; known through reports by Sureśvara and Yāmuna.

name: Sundarapāṇḍya
summary: Early author to whom later commentators attribute the three verses quoted at the end of Śaṅkara's BSBh 1.1.4 (that once 'I am the existent Brahman' is known, there is nothing further to be done, and the knower-status lasts only until the self is known).

name: Guhadeva
summary: Ancient Vedāntin named by Rāmānuja (Vedārthasaṅgraha) among the earlier teachers (with Bodhāyana, Ṭaṅka, Dramiḍa, Kapardin and Bharuci).

name: Kapardin
summary: Ancient Vedāntin named by Rāmānuja among the earlier teachers.

name: Bharuci
summary: Ancient Vedāntin named by Rāmānuja among the earlier teachers; possibly the same as the Dharmaśāstra commentator Bhāruci (uncertain).

name: Gauḍapāda

tradition.text: disciple of Śuka; paramaguru of Śaṅkara

notes: Also credited (traditional) with Śākta works (Subhagodaya, Śrīvidyāratnasūtras) and an Uttaragītā commentary. Whether he is the same person as the author of the commentary on the Sāṃkhya Kārikā (src:samkhya-karika-bhasya-gaudapada) is doubted by most scholars.
summary: Author of the Māṇḍūkya Kārikā; teacher of Govinda, Śaṅkara's teacher, and in the paramparā disciple of Śuka; first systematic exponent of non-origination (ajātivāda) and asparśa-yoga.

name: Govinda Bhagavatpāda
summary: Śaṅkara's guru, disciple of Gauḍapāda; the Śaṅkaradigvijaya places him in a cave on the Narmadā where he initiated Śaṅkara into sannyāsa, and identifies him with Patañjali/Ādiśeṣa.

name: Śaṅkara (Ādi Śaṅkarācārya)

tradition.text: 788–820 CE in the commonest traditional reckoning; 509–477 BCE in the Kāñcī and Dvārakā maṭha reckonings

scholarly.text: c. 700–750 CE (Hacker, Nakamura); other scholars up to c. 800

places: Kedāranātha or Kāñcī (death, by differing accounts)

realization_account.text: The Śaṅkaradigvijaya tells that Śaṅkara, an only son of Śivaguru and Āryāmbā, obtained his mother's consent to renounce when a crocodile seized him in the river; that Govinda initiated him; that Vyāsa appeared to him at Kāśī and extended his life from sixteen to thirty-two years; and that he ascended the Sarvajña-pīṭha in Kashmir.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Scholarly consensus (Hacker, Mayeda, Ingalls) accepts the BSBh, the principal Upaniṣad commentaries, the Gītā commentary and the Upadeśasāhasrī; most prakaraṇas and stotras are doubted.
summary: The systematizer of Advaita Vedānta: commentator on the Brahma Sūtras, the principal Upaniṣads and the Gītā, author of the Upadeśasāhasrī; in the tradition's account a child renunciant from Kālaṭi who studied under Govinda, debated Maṇḍana Miśra, founded the four āmnāya maṭhas and the Daśanāmī order, revived Vedic dharma and died at thirty-two.

name: Padmapāda
summary: Senior disciple of Śaṅkara, author of the Pañcapādikā, root of the Vivaraṇa school; in the tradition's account named 'lotus-foot' because lotuses sprang up under his feet when he crossed the Gaṅgā at his guru's call, and first head of the Govardhana maṭha at Purī.

name: Sureśvara
notes: Identity with Maṇḍana: the tradition's account (Śaṅkaradigvijaya). Most modern scholars (Hiriyanna, Kuppuswami Sastri) hold them distinct because their doctrines differ (e.g. on prasaṅkhyāna and on works).
summary: Disciple of Śaṅkara, author of the Naiṣkarmyasiddhi and of the Vārttikas on Śaṅkara's Bṛhadāraṇyaka and Taittirīya commentaries; exponent of the semblance theory (ābhāsa-vāda) and of knowledge alone as liberating; in the tradition's account first head of Śṛṅgeri and identical with Maṇḍana Miśra after his defeat in debate.

name: Hastāmalaka
summary: Disciple of Śaṅkara; in the tradition's account a seemingly dull boy who, asked 'who are you?', answered with the verses of the Hastāmalakīya, knowing the self as clearly as 'an āmalaka fruit in the hand'; first head of the Dvārakā (Śāradā) maṭha.

name: Toṭaka (Toṭakācārya)
notes: Not to be confused with Ānandagiri (Ānandajñāna), the 13th-c. commentator.
summary: Disciple of Śaṅkara, author (tradition) of the Toṭakāṣṭaka in praise of his guru and the Śrutisārasamuddharaṇa; in the tradition's account a devoted servant (called Giri) whose realization came through the guru's grace, first head of Jyotirmaṭh.

name: Maṇḍana Miśra

realization_account.text: In the Śaṅkaradigvijaya, Maṇḍana, a householder ritualist and disciple of Kumārila, debated Śaṅkara for many days with his wife Ubhaya Bhāratī as judge; defeated, he took sannyāsa as Sureśvara.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Mīmāṃsaka and Advaitin, author of the Brahmasiddhi (and of the Mīmāṃsā works Vidhiviveka and Bhāvanāviveka, the Vibhramaviveka and the grammatical Sphoṭasiddhi); held avidyā to reside in the jīvas, the need for prasaṅkhyāna after verbal knowledge, and a helpful role for works; in the tradition's account defeated by Śaṅkara at Māhiṣmatī and became Sureśvara.

name: Ubhaya Bhāratī
summary: Wife of Maṇḍana Miśra who, in the tradition's account, judged the debate between Śaṅkara and her husband by the fading of the garlands they wore, then herself debated Śaṅkara; venerated as Sarasvatī (Śāradā), associated with the Śāradā shrine at Śṛṅgeri.

name: Sarvajñātman

tradition.text: disciple of Sureśvara; claimed by the Kāñcī tradition as an early pontiff

summary: Author of the Saṃkṣepaśārīraka; disciple of 'Deveśvara', traditionally identified with Sureśvara; held pure consciousness to be both the locus and object of ignorance.

name: Vācaspati Miśra

scholarly.text: 9th or 10th c. CE (Nyāyasūcīnibandha dated 898, read as 841 or 976 CE)

summary: Polymath of Mithilā who commented on the works of six schools; his Bhāmatī on Śaṅkara's BSBh founded the Bhāmatī line of Advaita, and his lost Tattvasamīkṣā commented on Maṇḍana's Brahmasiddhi.

name: Amalānanda
summary: Author of the Vedāntakalpataru on the Bhāmatī and of the Śāstradarpaṇa; 13th-century Advaitin at the Yādava court.

name: Prakāśātman
summary: Author of the Pañcapādikāvivaraṇa, founder of the Vivaraṇa school.

name: Akhaṇḍānanda
summary: Author of the Tattvadīpana on the Vivaraṇa.

name: Vimuktātman
summary: Author of the Iṣṭasiddhi, defending indescribable ignorance and the self as pure experience.

name: Ānandabodha (Bhaṭṭāraka)
summary: Dialectical Advaitin, author of the Nyāyamakaranda (and the Nyāyadīpāvalī and Pramāṇamālā).

name: Śrīharṣa
summary: Poet and dialectician, author of the Khaṇḍanakhaṇḍakhādya and of the mahākāvya Naiṣadhīyacarita; demolished the Nyāya definitions in defence of Advaita.

name: Citsukha
summary: Dialectical Advaitin, author of the Tattvapradīpikā and of commentaries on the Khaṇḍana, the Brahmasiddhi and the Nyāyamakaranda; pupil of Jñānottama.

name: Jñānottama
summary: Advaitin, teacher of Citsukha, author of a commentary (Candrikā) on the Naiṣkarmyasiddhi.

name: Ānandagiri (Ānandajñāna)
summary: 13th-century glossator of nearly all of Śaṅkara's commentaries (Nyāyanirṇaya on the BSBh; ṭīkās on the Upaniṣad and Gītā bhāṣyas) and of Sureśvara's Vārttika; his glosses name Bhartṛprapañca as the opponent refuted there.

name: Govindānanda
summary: Author of the Ratnaprabhā gloss on Śaṅkara's BSBh.

name: Vidyāraṇya
notes: Identity with the minister Mādhava is the tradition's; scholars debate it.
summary: Pontiff of Śṛṅgeri (d. 1386), author of the Pañcadaśī, the Jīvanmuktiviveka, the Vivaraṇaprameyasaṅgraha and the Anubhūtiprakāśa; in the tradition identified with Mādhava, minister of the founders of Vijayanagara and brother of Sāyaṇa, and so credited with the Sarvadarśanasaṅgraha and the Śaṅkaradigvijaya.

name: Bhāratītīrtha
summary: Śṛṅgeri pontiff of the 14th century, associate of Vidyāraṇya; credited with part of the Pañcadaśī, the Vaiyāsikanyāyamālā and (by some) the Dṛg-Dṛśya Viveka.

name: Śaṅkarānanda
summary: 14th-c. Advaitin saluted as guru in the opening verse of the Pañcadaśī; author of the Ātmapurāṇa and of Upaniṣad and Gītā commentaries.

name: Vidyāśaṅkara (Vidyātīrtha)
summary: Śṛṅgeri pontiff of the 14th c., remembered in the Śṛṅgeri tradition as Vidyāraṇya's teacher; the Vidyāśaṅkara temple at Śṛṅgeri commemorates him.

name: Prakāśānanda
notes: Gauḍīya hagiography (Caitanya Caritāmṛta) tells of a Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī of Vārāṇasī won over by Caitanya; identity with this author is uncertain.
summary: Author of the Vedāntasiddhāntamuktāvalī, the chief exponent of dṛṣṭi-sṛṣṭi-vāda and eka-jīva-vāda.

name: Madhusūdana Sarasvatī
summary: Bengal-born Advaitin of Vārāṇasī, author of the Advaitasiddhi (against Vyāsatīrtha's Nyāyāmṛta), the Gūḍhārthadīpikā, the Siddhāntabindu, the Bhaktirasāyana, the Vedāntakalpalatikā, the Advaitaratnarakṣaṇa and the Prasthānabheda; joined rigorous Advaita dialectic with ardent devotion to Kṛṣṇa.

name: Brahmānanda Sarasvatī
summary: Author of the Laghucandrikā ('Gauḍa-Brahmānandī') on the Advaitasiddhi and of the Nyāyaratnāvalī on the Siddhāntabindu.

name: Appayya Dīkṣita
summary: Polymath of Tamil Nadu, author of the Siddhāntaleśasaṅgraha, the Kalpataruparimala (completing the Bhāmatī chain), the Nyāyarakṣāmaṇi, works in Mīmāṃsā and poetics, and the Śivārkamaṇidīpikā on Śrīkaṇṭha's Śaiva Vedānta; an Advaitin devoted to Śiva.

name: Sadānanda (Yogīndra)
summary: Author of the Vedāntasāra.

name: Nṛsiṃha Sarasvatī (author of the Subodhinī)
summary: Commentator on the Vedāntasāra (Subodhinī). Distinct from Narasiṃha Sarasvatī of the Datta tradition.

name: Rāmatīrtha
summary: Commentator on the Vedāntasāra (Vidvanmanorañjanī) and on the Upadeśasāhasrī. Distinct from the recent Swami Rama Tirtha.

name: Dharmarāja Adhvarīndra
summary: Author of the Vedāntaparibhāṣā, manual of Advaita epistemology.

name: Rāmakṛṣṇa Adhvarin
summary: Son of Dharmarāja, author of the Śikhāmaṇi on the Vedāntaparibhāṣā.

name: Nṛsiṃhāśrama
summary: 16th-c. Advaitin of the Vivaraṇa line, author of the Vedāntatattvaviveka, the Advaitadīpikā and the Bhedadhikkāra.

name: Lakṣmīdhara Kavi
summary: Author of the Advaitamakaranda.

name: Gaṅgādharendra Sarasvatī
summary: Author of the Svārājyasiddhi.

name: Sadāśiva Brahmendra
summary: Avadhūta and poet of the Kāverī region (c. 17th–18th c.), author of the Ātmavidyāvilāsa, a Brahmasūtra commentary (Brahmatattvaprakāśikā), a Yoga Sūtra commentary and Sanskrit songs; remembered as a jīvanmukta who wandered naked and silent.

name: Upaniṣad Brahmayogin (Upaniṣad Brahmendra)
summary: 18th-c. Advaitin of Kāñcī who wrote commentaries on all 108 Upaniṣads of the Muktikā canon.

name: Śrīdhara Svāmin
summary: Advaita renunciant (associated with Purī) whose commentaries on the Bhāgavata (Bhāvārthadīpikā), the Gītā (Subodhinī) and the Viṣṇu Purāṇa combine non-dualism with devotion.

name: Tāṇḍavarāya Svāmī
summary: Author of the Tamil Advaita classic Kaivalya Navanītam.

name: Haritāyana
summary: Narrator of the Tripura Rahasya, conveying Dattātreya's teaching to Paraśurāma.

name: Swami Satchidanandendra Sarasvati
summary: Advaitin of Holenarsipur (1880–1975) who argued that Śaṅkara's avidyā is superimposition itself, not a positive root-ignorance, and that post-Śaṅkara schools (esp. the Vivaraṇa) diverged from him.

name: Candraśekhara Bhāratī III
summary: Pontiff of Śṛṅgeri (1892–1954), revered in the tradition as a jīvanmukta given to long absorption.

name: Candraśekharendra Sarasvatī
summary: Pontiff of the Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi pīṭha (1894–1994), teacher of Advaita and Vedic dharma.

name: Swami Chinmayananda
summary: Advaita teacher (1916–1993), disciple of Sivananda and Tapovan Maharaj, founder of the Chinmaya Mission, who taught the prasthāna-traya and prakaraṇas in English.

name: Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya)
summary: Advaita teacher (1930–2015) of the traditional method of teaching (sampradāya) through the texts; founder of the Arsha Vidya Gurukulam. Distinct from the 19th-c. founder of the Ārya Samāj.
